observations.name: Process Injection
observations.justification: The malware string 'OpenProcess' was found in the binary. This string is characteristic of Process Injection behavior. The presence of this specific string alone (no other Process Injection-related string corroborates it) indicates the malware has capabilities associated with this technique, but with less certainty than a corroborated combination would.

observations.name: Process Discovery
observations.justification: The API function 'CreateToolhelp32Snapshot' is imported by the binary. This API is commonly used to perform Process Discovery. Importing this function alone (no other Process Discovery-related import corroborates it) indicates the malware has the capability to execute this technique, but with less certainty than a corroborated combination would.

observations.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
observations.justification: The malware string 'CreateProcessW' was found in the binary, alongside 1 other string(s) also characteristic of Command and Scripting Interpreter. Multiple corroborating strings, not this one in isolation, is what makes this a strong signal.

observations.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
observations.justification: The malware string 'ShellExecuteW' was found in the binary, alongside 1 other string(s) also characteristic of Command and Scripting Interpreter. Multiple corroborating strings, not this one in isolation, is what makes this a strong signal.

observations.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
observations.justification: The API functions CreateProcessW, ShellExecuteW are all imported by the binary. This combination is characteristic of Command and Scripting Interpreter — multiple corroborating APIs together, not one import in isolation, is what makes this a strong signal.

observations.name: Privilege Escalation
observations.justification: The API function 'OpenProcessToken' is imported by the binary. This API is commonly used to perform Privilege Escalation. Importing this function alone (no other Privilege Escalation-related import corroborates it) indicates the malware has the capability to execute this technique, but with less certainty than a corroborated combination would.
